subject: Chunked transfer rendezvous timeouts causing streaming stalls - Exec escalation
messages:
From: Michael Torres <michael.torres@atlasfinance.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: SRE Team <sre@atlasfinance.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Live stream timeouts & partial responses affecting 2FA flows

Camila —

We saw repeated WebSocket timeouts and truncated chunked responses during peak hours this morning (08:30–09:15 PST). End user flows that rely on token streaming for the 2FA prompt are timing out intermittently and failing open. We captured a few traces and see long gaps (10–20s) with TCP keepalive still upstream. Attached is a small log snippet and a pcap our SRE captured.

Can you confirm whether this is on your side (proxy / chunk assembly) or our connectivity? We need an ETA — this is impacting our transactional throughput and is currently blocking an urgent release.

— Michael
Senior Platform Engineer, Atlas Finance

From: camila_reyes@redwood.com
To: Michael Torres <michael.torres@atlasfinance.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-29T10:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Live stream timeouts & partial responses affecting 2FA flows

Michael —

Thanks for the artifacts. We're looking into this immediately. Initial hypothesis: a rendezvous between our edge chunk-assembler and the customer's proxy is triggering a read timeout when mid-stream ACK patterns change under high concurrency. That can surface as long silent intervals followed by a stream tear-down.

Action plan (short):
- I have Dev running a targeted repro on the same model / input shape and concurrency you reported.
- Grace is pulling per-route tokenization and keepalive metrics to see if there was a sudden shape/regime shift.
- We'll share traces and a timeline within 90 minutes.

Can you also share whether you have a proxy idle-timeout configured (nginx / envoy) or if the client closes aggressively? It helps to know whether the gap is initiated upstream.

Regards,
Camila Reyes
Account Lead — Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: rendezvous-trace-20261130.zip)

From: dev_patel@redwood.com
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-29T10:58:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Live stream timeouts & partial responses affecting 2FA flows

On Mon, Nov 29, 2026 at 10:04 AM camila_reyes@redwood.com wrote:
> Initial hypothesis: a rendezvous between our edge chunk-assembler and the customer's proxy is triggering a read timeout when mid-stream ACK patterns change under high concurrency.

I've reproduced a similar gap locally when the client half-closes the socket between chunks (emulated flaky mobile). The runtime currently waits up to 30s for the next message frame before triggering an inbound timeout; the proxy layer has a default 15s idle. The mismatch means our runtime can appear to 'hang' while the proxy times out and tears the connection, resulting in truncated responses and a 502 upstream.

Short-term mitigations I can push as a config toggle (no code):
- Reduce runtime idle read window from 30s -> 8s for the affected route.
- Enable early chunk flush on partial KV cache availability to avoid long quiet windows.

I'll deploy the toggle to a canary pool in us-west and report back within 45 minutes.

— Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime

From: Michael Torres <michael.torres@atlasfinance.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: SRE Team <sre@atlasfinance.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T12:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Live stream timeouts & partial responses affecting 2FA flows

Thanks — we do have an Envoy route idle_timeout set to 10s for these endpoints to conserve connections on our edge. We can temporarily increase to 30s, but we'd prefer Redwood to avoid introducing latency for our clients.

If you can shorten your runtime window and enable early chunk flush that would be ideal. Please confirm when the canary is up and if you need us to generate synthetic traffic.

— Michael

From: camila_reyes@redwood.com
To: senior_leaders@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-29T14:20:00-08:00
Subject: FYI / escalating: Atlas Finance streaming timeouts impacting production throughput

Team —

Looping in Marissa and leadership due to customer impact and potential SLA exposure. Key points:
- Incident: repeated WebSocket idle gaps leading to connection termination and truncated chunked responses for Atlas Finance (prod-us).
- Business impact: intermittent failure of critical 2FA prompt flows during morning peak; observed throughput degradation ~12% and error-rate spike to 4.6% on the route between 08:30–09:15 PST.
- Immediate mitigations in flight: canary toggle to reduce runtime idle window, enable early-flush, and coordination with Atlas SRE to relax Envoy idle_timeout if necessary.

Request: exec visibility — if we need to offer credits or SLA exceptions, want alignment before committing. Marissa, can you advise on threshold for proactive crediting in similar incidents?

Thanks,
Camila

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com, senior_leaders@redwood.com
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-30T09:06:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FYI / escalating: Atlas Finance streaming timeouts impacting production throughput

On Tue, Nov 30, 2026 at 02:20 PM camila_reyes@redwood.com wrote:
> Request: exec visibility — if we need to offer credits or SLA exceptions, want alignment before committing.

Camila / Team —

Please prioritize resolving the customer-visible error spike; operationally we should run the canary and determine blast radius. If the canary shows improvement and Atlas wants a temporary increase on their Envoy idle_timeout, prefer we avoid credits unless postmortem shows a platform regression. If the platform change is required (we initiated a config with risk), offer a standard 10% pro-rata credit for the window while we rolled out the fix. Escalate to Legal only if Customer requests contract amendment.

I'll join the postmortem review tomorrow.

— Marissa
VP, Platform Operations

From: Michael Torres <michael.torres@atlasfinance.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: SRE Team <sre@atlasfinance.com>, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-01T17:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Live stream timeouts — confirmation and follow-up

Camila / Team —

Canary looks good after your runtime toggle; gaps reduced and client-side errors dropped to 0.6%. We increased Envoy idle_timeout to 25s as a belt-and-suspenders measure while you push the broader runtime tuning. We did observe one long-tail trace where packet reordering at our edge correlated with a 6s gap — attaching the snippet.

Next steps:
- Redwood: include a permanent route profile recommendation for customers with mobile-heavy clients (docs + Console suggestion).
- Atlas: will run a week of extended traffic and revert if we see regression.

Thanks for fast turnaround — please include the incident timeline and recommended config changes in the postmortem link you shared.

— Michael
